title: Greedy & Intervals Journey
description: Greedy choice arguments, reachability, scheduling, interval merging, and overlap queries.

prerequisites: Heap basics for deadline and overlap problems
journey.outcome: Explain why a local choice is safe, and make endpoint and overlap conventions explicit before processing intervals.

connections.jump-game: Track the farthest position reachable from the processed prefix. An unreachable index cannot contribute a jump, so expanding the frontier requires a clear feasibility invariant.
connections.jump-game-ii: Keep the same reachability frontier but group positions by number of jumps. Finishing one reachable layer commits one jump and moves to the farthest next frontier.
connections.gas-station: Use a failed prefix to eliminate several starting candidates at once. A negative running balance invalidates every start inside that failed segment, while total fuel still determines overall feasibility.
connections.candy: One directional greedy pass cannot satisfy constraints from both neighbors. Combine left-to-right and right-to-left requirements without erasing a larger requirement from the other direction.
connections.hand-of-straights: Choose the smallest remaining value because it cannot belong after a missing smaller value in its group. Consume one consecutive group at a time while respecting duplicate counts.
connections.partition-labels: Extend the current segment until it includes the final occurrence of every character already inside it. Cutting before that boundary would violate the partition constraint.
connections.fractional-knapsack: Use value per unit weight only because fractions are allowed. Contrast this exchange argument with 0/1 knapsack, where indivisible choices can invalidate the same greedy ordering.
connections.job-sequencing: Add deadlines to valuable unit-time choices. Sorting by deadline and retaining the strongest feasible profit set in a min-heap separates scheduling feasibility from profit priority.
connections.merge-intervals: Sort by interval start so only the latest merged range can overlap the next range. Preserve the maximum end rather than assuming later input has a later endpoint.
connections.insert-interval: Reuse merging when the existing intervals are already sorted and disjoint. Copy ranges before the insertion, merge the overlap block, then append the untouched suffix.
connections.non-overlapping-intervals: Change the objective from representing the union to selecting compatible intervals. Keeping the earliest finish leaves the most room for future choices and yields minimum removals.
connections.meeting-rooms: Use sorted adjacent comparisons to test whether one resource can serve every interval. Decide explicitly whether a meeting ending at a time can share a room with one starting then.
connections.meeting-rooms-ii: Replace the one-room feasibility question with peak simultaneous demand. A heap of ending times or a sorted event sweep tracks how many resources remain occupied.
connections.minimum-interval-to-include-each-query: Interview stretch: answer point queries offline in sorted order. A heap ranks eligible intervals by length while their right endpoints determine when they expire.
